title: SIG Questionnaire Walkthrough - Lyra Insurance
summary: Redwood team walked Lyra Insurance through the SIG/CAIQ questionnaire items that are most relevant: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 posture, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit log retention and access, encryption at rest/in transit (KMS/HSM), and data residency options (EU). Discussed evidence artifacts (SOC2 report, pen test, architecture diagrams), how to upload evidence to Lyra's intake portal, and agreed on next steps for delivering documents and scheduling a follow-up in two weeks.
topics: Data residency and Private VPC option
next_steps: Jordan to upload SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summary to Lyra intake by 2026-04-01
Samira to share architecture diagram and KMS key management diagram by 2026-03-30
Lyra to confirm which CAIQ sections require company-specific evidence by 2026-03-29
Schedule follow-up to review submitted evidence week of 2026-04-06
action_items: Jordan Ellis - Send SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) - due 2026-04-01
Samira Patel - Provide encryption/KMS diagram and key lifecycle doc - due 2026-03-30
Miguel Torres - Share link to security whitepaper and CAIQ pre-map spreadsheet - due 2026-03-27
Carlos Mendes - Provide Lyra vendor intake URL and list of mandatory evidence fields - due 2026-03-29
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Miguel (CSM), Carlos (Lyra), Priya (Lyra), Ethan (Lyra), Nora (Lyra legal)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the SIG walkthrough. Uh, Miguel, do you want to intro briefly?
[00:12] Miguel: Yeah hi all — Miguel from Red wood CSM, we'll help manage the evidence handoff and timelines.
[00:20] Carlos: Thanks, we got a full panel from Lyra — I'm Carlos, head of IT risk. Priya is here for architecture, Ethan procurement and Nora legal.
[00:28] Jordan: Great, objective today is to go line by line over the high-risk SIG and CAIQ items you flagged, align on what Redwood can provide from a hosted and private deployment perspective and agree next steps. We'll call out artifacts you can expect — SOC2, pen test, infra diagrams, etc.
[00:44] Priya: We prioritized SOC2, encryption, and audit logs. We also have a couple of questions about VPC/private deployment for EU data residency.
[00:52] Samira: Awesome, we'll start with the SOC 2 and ISO posture. Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II last quarter, we'll share the report; for ISO, we have an ISO 27001 alignment doc — it's not certified yet but we maintain controls mapped to ISO.
[01:12] Priya: When you say "share the report", can you confirm redactions? We need evidence of coverage for storage, access control, incident response.
[01:22] Jordan: Yes, we'll provide a redacted SOC2 report and a cover letter explaining scope — hosted API, control plane, and data handling. We'll also include our incident response runbook summary and recent tabletop results.
[01:36] Nora: On legal side, we need the report and the pen test summary. Also please include dates and control owners.
[01:46] Samira: Got it. We have a third-party pentest from last quarter, summary and remediation log. Full report is under NDA; we can provide redacted findings and proof of remediation.
[01:58] Carlos: Next on our list is SSO and RBAC. Lyra uses SAML SSO via Okta and SCIM provisioning. We also require role-based access with least privilege.
[02:12] Samira: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO, IdP initiated and SP initiated. We also support SCIM for automated provisioning and deprovisioning. For RBAC, we support role templates and custom roles; we can map Lyra roles to our admin/developer/read-only roles. I'll share sample SCIM mapping.
[02:32] Priya: How granular is the RBAC? Can we restrict access to logs and PII by role?
[02:40] Samira: Yes, audit log access is gated by roles; you can restrict who can view raw request/response data. For hosted customers we also offer a dedicated role that limits visibility to metadata only. Note, though, that high-sensitivity data controls are stronger on Private deployment.
[02:58] Ethan: For procurement we need the SAML implementation guide and an example SAML metadata file.
[03:06] Jordan: We'll add those to the package.
[03:10] [04:00] Samira: Next — audit logs and retention. Redwood collects structured audit logs: authentication events, API requests, admin actions, and system events. Default retention on hosted is 90 days; we offer extended retention and log forwarding to your SIEM via secure webhooks or syslog.
[04:20] Priya: Do you provide immutable logs or tamper-evidence? We need cryptographic integrity for some logs.
[04:28] Samira: We support append-only storage with signed log digests for our critical audit streams; for stronger guarantees customers often stream logs into their own AWS account using Kinesis or to an S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled.
[04:44] Carlos: Good. About encryption: we need details on encryption at rest, in transit and key management.
[04:50] Samira: Encryption in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. At rest we use AES-256. Key management is via AWS KMS for hosted customers; keys are service-managed by default. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and HSM integrations. We'll share a KMS diagram and KMS lifecycle doc.
[05:10] Priya: Do you support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) and rotation policies?
[05:14] Samira: Yes BYOK for dedicated and private; keys rotate per your policy and we can supply rotation logs. For hosted, we support customer-managed KMS through cross-account key usage in many cases — detail depends on contract.
[05:28] Nora: We need a statement about where keys are stored and whether Redwood staff can access plaintext data.
[05:34] Jordan: Short answer: Redwood staff do not have access to customer plaintext in systems where CMK is enforced; we'll provide an access control statement and diagram for the control plane that shows separation of duties.
[05:46] [08:00] Miguel: On data residency, Lyra mentioned EU requirement. We can deploy in EU region; our private deployment option puts compute in your VPC and data never leaves your AWS account. For hosted EU tenancy we store customer data in EU regions and provide data residency attestation.
[08:24] Priya: What's the latency tradeoff if we pick EU hosted versus cross-region?
[08:30] Samira: Minimal for EU customers — sub 100ms for typical gen workloads from EU offices. If you want absolute control, Private VPC will keep everything in-region with no cross-region control plane linkage. We'll provide benchmark numbers.
[08:44] Carlos: On the SIG itself, we've pre-marked around 40 fields as high priority. Which fields do you want completed by Redwood versus where you'll need Lyra-specific evidence?
[08:58] Jordan: We'll complete the coverage columns for technical controls that are Red wood-managed: encryption, infrastructure, vulnerability mgmt, pen test. For process items that require Lyra-specific evidence — e.g., data classification choices, retention windows, contractual commitments — we'll note what evidence you need to upload. We'll also pre-fill CAIQ mapping for clarity.
[09:18] Priya: For example, CAIQ 3.5 asks for data flow diagrams. Can you provide a data flow diagram and a redwood-hosted example with EU flow?
[09:26] Samira: Yes, we'll provide a redacted data flow diagram showing control plane separation, KV cache handling, and data egress paths. Note that some internal names may be redacted in shared artifacts.
[09:36] Ethan: Procurement question — what's the typical SLA for evidence turnaround?
[09:40] Jordan: For standard requests we aim to provide most artifacts within 5 business days; full pen test and legal docs sometimes require NDA and can take longer. For this engagement, we suggested 7-10 business days for the initial package.
[09:54] Nora: We'll need a clear list of evidence filenames, formats, and contact for NDA.
[09:58] Miguel: I'll send a packet via secure link and we can sign an NDA if needed. We'll include a CAIQ prefilled spreadsheet.
[10:10] [12:00] Priya: A couple of technical clarifications — how do you handle KV cache and PII in logs? I know you mentioned KV cache earlier.
[12:18] Samira: The KV cache is in-memory on the inference nodes and not persisted to long-term storage; we scrub PII from logs in the default hosted configuration but for regulated customers we recommend Private deployment where you control persistence. We also offer retention policies that drop request/response payloads after X hours.
[12:36] Priya: Can you run a token-level redaction before logging?
[12:40] Samira: We have hooks for pre-log filters in our integration library — you can mask tokens client-side or set server-side rules. We'll share examples for the SDK.
[12:52] Carlos: What about access to model prompts and responses for debugging? Who at Redwood can see that?
[12:58] Jordan: By default, only system processes have capability but engineers can access logs for debugging under strict RBAC and with audit trail. For customers requiring zero-visibility, Private options with CMK and no control plane access are recommended.
[13:16] [18:00] Miguel: Regarding SIG evidence upload: many customers prefer we upload docs directly to their vendor portal. We can do that if you provide the portal link and instructions. Alternatively, we can provide a secure temporary S3 link or an encrypted zip under NDA.
[18:28] Ethan: We'll send the Lyra vendor intake URL. We also need a checklist for the files: SOC2, pen test summary, data flow diagram, KMS diagram, SAML metadata, SCIM mapping, architecture diagram, CAIQ prefill.
[18:42] Jordan: We'll produce a checklist and a folder with those artifacts.
[18:48] Priya: A question about log forwarding: can you forward to our Splunk instance in our AWS account?
[18:54] Samira: Yes, we support cross-account delivery via Kinesis or S3 with role assumption. We can also deliver syslog/HTTPS events to your SIEM; we'll share configuration steps for Splunk HEC.
[19:10] Nora: Legal flags — do you have a data processing addendum and standard data residency language?
[19:16] Jordan: Yes, DPA is standard; we'll include data residency clauses and SCCs for EU transfers if needed. For Private deployments SCCs are less relevant since data stays in your account.
[19:28] [26:00] Priya: Can you summarize the evidence you'll provide in the first packet?
[26:08] Miguel: Sure — SOC2 Type II redacted report, pen test executive summary and remediation log, CAIQ prefilled spreadsheet, redacted data flow and KMS diagrams, SAML/SCIM implementation guide, architecture diagram, and a security whitepaper. Links will be delivered via secure share.
[26:26] Carlos: We'll need dates and point contacts on each artifact.
[26:30] Miguel: We'll annotate each file with owner and date.
[26:36] Jordan: On timing, target to send initial package by 2026-04-01; Samira will send technical diagrams this week.
[26:46] Samira: I'll also include examples of role mappings for RBAC and recommended least-privilege templates.
[26:54] [33:00] Priya: A small technical ask: we need to validate that key operations (encrypt/decrypt) are logged and that logs show key usage without revealing key material.
[33:12] Samira: Yes KMS usage is logged via CloudTrail events; we can provide sample CloudTrail entries with redacted ARNs showing key usage. We'll also provide rotation history.
[33:28] Nora: Another legal note — do you have cyber insurance details and coverage limits?
[33:34] Jordan: Yes we carry cyber insurance; we'll provide a certificate of insurance with limits and effective dates.
[33:40] Ethan: Any limitations on export control or geofencing for models? Some of our use cases need model locality.
[33:48] Samira: We support model pinning and running specific model variants in-region. Some open models have licensing terms; we'll surface any export or licensing constraints per model in the catalog.
[33:58] [40:00] Carlos: On remediation evidence for pen test, we need to see closure tickets or tracking.
[40:06] Samira: We'll supply a redacted remediation tracker that maps findings to JIRA tickets and timelines. Sensitive details redacted.
[40:16] Priya: For the CAIQ answers that Redwood marks as partial, can you add a note explaining what evidence is needed from us?
[40:22] Jordan: Absolutely — we'll annotate partials with a clear required evidence list.
[40:28] Miguel: Also offering to run a short joint workshop to walk Lyra's security team through the artifacts once uploaded. Would that help?
[40:34] Carlos: Yes please. We'll coordinate a follow-up session.
[40:38] [48:00] Jordan: Quick recap — we'll provide the evidence bundle by 2026-04-01, Samira will send technical diagrams by 2026-03-30, Miguel will share CAIQ prefill and secure upload link by 2026-03-27. Lyra to confirm mandatory fields and provide vendor intake URL by 2026-03-29. Follow-up meeting week of 2026-04-06 to review.
[48:18] Priya: Sounds good, thanks.
[48:22] Nora: One last thing — can you confirm retention SLA for audit logs if we ask for 7 years?
[48:30] Samira: Hosted option has constraints on default retention; for 7 years we recommend log forwarding to Lyra-managed S3 with Object Lock or Private deployment where retention policies are enforced in your account. We'll document the approach and cost implications.
[48:48] Ethan: Procurement will also need sample contract language on data residency.
[48:52] Jordan: We'll include that in the packet.
[48:56] Miguel: I'll send calendar invite for a follow-up and the secure share link today.
[49:06] Carlos: Thanks all.
[49:10] Jordan: Thanks team — we'll follow up in writing with the checklist and links.
[49:18] End of recording (58:02).

Notes/links referenced: SOC2 redacted report link (will be provided via secure share), Pen test exec summary (NDA required for full report), CAIQ prefill spreadsheet (link to be sent), SAML implementation guide (attachment), sample SCIM mapping (attachment), KMS lifecycle diagram (attachment).

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present ("Red wood" for Redwood, "KV cache" sometimes mis-transcribed), speaker labels are mostly accurate but there are a few overlapped segments.
